title: Consumer Outcomes on Digital Platforms
summary: How platform design, personalisation and data use shape consumer decisions, the risks of harm and exclusion, and the evidence supervisors should seek on outcomes in embedded journeys.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How platform design, personalisation and data use shape consumer decisions, the risks of harm and exclusion, and the evidence supervisors should seek on outcomes in embedded journeys.
Learning Objectives: Identify consumer harms from choice architecture, dark patterns and frictionless credit
Assess disclosure, suitability and complaints handling in embedded journeys
Evaluate the financial inclusion benefits and risks of platform finance
Syllabus: Choice architecture, defaults and dark patterns
Embedded credit and buy now, pay later products
Personalised pricing, profiling and fair treatment
Who owns the complaint: redress across the partnership chain
Intended Audience: Supervisors of banks, payment and e-money institutions, lenders and insurers that partner with platforms or distribute through them
Policy, innovation and authorisation staff dealing with new entrants, perimeter questions and open finance
Senior managers coordinating with competition, data protection and consumer authorities
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of banking, payments or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
